finding.claim: Xxh32::update computes the buffer-fit check using u32 arithmetic on a truncated input length. For slices of about 4 GiB or more, the check passes incorrectly and copy_from_slice copies the full untruncated slice into the 16-byte self.mem buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write in release builds.
finding.source: Caller-supplied byte slice passed to Xxh32::update (src/xxh32.rs:102) or io::Write::write (src/xxh32.rs:198-201) with len >= ~2^32-15 in a single call
finding.sink: src/utils.rs:48 ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(src.as_ptr(), self.ptr.add(self.offset), len) with len = src.len(); destination is Xxh32.mem (src/xxh32.rs:84, 16 bytes)

trace.note: calls self.update(buf) with the full slice
total_len wrapping add with input.len() as u32 (truncation)
guard (mem_size + input.len() as u32) < 16 wrongly true for len=2^32 (truncates to 0) or len near 2^32 where sum wraps
copy_from_slice(input) on the first branch, using full untruncated input.len()
debug_assert bounds check; compiled out in release
copy_nonoverlapping writes len bytes starting at self.mem

finding.guards_checked: xxh32.rs:106 comparison uses truncated u32 arithmetic and is not a real bounds check; utils.rs:45 debug_assert only active in debug builds; no release-mode length check on the input before the copy; no Cargo.toml so release profile not confirmed. Sibling xxh64.rs:119-124 and xxh3.rs:890-898 use usize/bounded values and are SAFE.
